reason: E2 directly supports stress relief and microstructural changes from low-temperature annealing in a related EHEA, but the cited evidence does not address in-situ application, AlCrFeNiSi, or the specific mechanism of dislocation rearrangement without recrystallization. E1 and E3 provide no direct support for the key premises.
premises: Low-temperature annealing (≤700 °C) relieves residual stresses in additively manufactured high-entropy alloys.
In-situ annealing can refine microstructure and homogenize grain size across the build height.
Reduced dislocation density from annealing improves ductility without sacrificing yield strength.
The proposed mechanism (limited diffusion/dislocation rearrangement) operates without full recrystallization at ≤700 °C.
The intervention is applicable to AlCrFeNiSi processed by laser powder-bed fusion.
